db32bc6b2d.q: What is DOT Blitz Week and when does it occur in 2024?
db32bc6b2d.a: DOT Blitz Week, officially known as the Commercial Vehicle Safety Alliance International Road Check, is a 72-hour concentrated inspection period happening May 12th through the 14th. During this period, inspectors across North America focus specifically on driver compliance and vehicle safety.
db32bc6b2d.e: Episode 30: DOT Blitz Week: What Shippers and Carriers Need to Know

d1388b80dd.q: Why is DOT Blitz Week considered a critical challenge for carriers in the logistics industry?
d1388b80dd.a: Carriers are already running tight on hours with high expectations from brokers and customers, and equipment might be aging. During this concentrated 72-hour window where inspectors are specifically looking for violations, things that might get overlooked normally will not be, and getting sidelined or delayed can mess up your whole route for the week or even strand a load entirely.
d1388b80dd.e: Episode 30: DOT Blitz Week: What Shippers and Carriers Need to Know

0d75fd4ed8.q: What specific documentation and equipment checks are prioritized by inspectors during DOT Blitz Week?
0d75fd4ed8.a: Carriers must ensure correct documentation including CDL licenses, medical certificates, and electronic logs, with drivers aligned to hours of service requirements. Inspectors will closely evaluate brakes, lights, tires, and cargo securement, with even minor issues causing major delays.
0d75fd4ed8.e: Episode 30: DOT Blitz Week: What Shippers and Carriers Need to Know

b15fd4be92.q: What are the most common preventable mistakes carriers make before DOT Blitz Week?
b15fd4be92.a: Carriers should not defer maintenance—anything that has been pending needs to be handled before the week, including brake pads, tire tread, and brake lights, as these become automatic out-of-service violations during Blitz Week. Documentation gaps are another major issue, including ensuring ELD logs are synced, medical cards and paperwork are in order, and registration is current.
b15fd4be92.e: Episode 30: DOT Blitz Week: What Shippers and Carriers Need to Know

b19e960c8a.q: What proactive strategies should shippers implement to minimize disruptions during DOT Blitz Week?
b19e960c8a.a: Shippers should pre-book as much capacity as possible in advance rather than waiting until the day of or day before, work with the most reliable and trusted brokers and carriers in their network, build in buffer time for deliveries, and set clear expectations with customers about potential four-hour delays from inspections. Internal alignment across departments is also critical so that sales representatives understand DOT Blitz Week impacts.
b19e960c8a.e: Episode 30: DOT Blitz Week: What Shippers and Carriers Need to Know

ce9bd6666f.q: How can internal communication within a shipper organization reduce DOT Blitz Week disruptions?
ce9bd6666f.a: Sales representatives often lack awareness of DOT Blitz Week, leading them to promise quick deliveries without understanding the constraints. Ensuring all departments, especially those relying on freight movement, understand what is coming that week allows proper expectations to be set with customers on the front end, making everything run smoother for everybody.
ce9bd6666f.e: Episode 30: DOT Blitz Week: What Shippers and Carriers Need to Know

3464eb9d29.q: How have spot market rates changed in the freight industry over the past six to eight months compared to historical benchmarks?
3464eb9d29.a: The fastest climb in spot market rates ever experienced in the freight market has occurred over the last six to eight months, even challenging what was experienced during early COVID days. Spot rates are now 30% to 40% higher inclusive of fuel, and 20% to 30% higher excluding fuel compared to the previous year.
3464eb9d29.e: Episode 31: 2026 Mid-Year State of the Freight

8a8f3e4253.q: What regulatory and enforcement changes have most significantly impacted truck driver supply in recent years?
8a8f3e4253.a: Non-domicile CDLs exploded as a new entry channel during COVID, with tens of thousands of drivers entering the market through immigration and new avenues. Since FMCSA enforcement cracked down, these states ceased issuing non-domicile CDLs, causing tens of thousands of such drivers to leave the market—one of the biggest factors in capacity contraction.
8a8f3e4253.e: Episode 31: 2026 Mid-Year State of the Freight

ace1d3c746.q: What is the connection between electronic logging device fraud and artificially inflated freight capacity?
ace1d3c746.a: Electronic logging devices, manufactured by over 100 different companies and mostly self-certified by manufacturers, have enabled fraud where drivers can artificially reset their hours-of-service status. FMCSA has been decertifying many ELD devices that were artificially allowing drivers to drive beyond legal hours of service, thereby removing artificial capacity from the market.
ace1d3c746.e: Episode 31: 2026 Mid-Year State of the Freight

bec9b5a858.q: How is AI-driven data center infrastructure development affecting freight demand in the flatbed sector?
bec9b5a858.a: Flatbed freight demand is being driven by AI-related data center buildouts and multi-billion dollar data center developments, with steel and components requiring transportation. Forecasts suggest this buildout will not slow down for 12 to 18 months, though the ultimate duration depends on where AI demand stabilizes.
bec9b5a858.e: Episode 31: 2026 Mid-Year State of the Freight

7677ee2524.q: What inventory dynamics are emerging in U.S. retail, and what freight demand implications do they signal?
7677ee2524.a: Inventory-to-sales ratios in the U.S. are now at their lowest point since early COVID around 2021, which is teeing up an inventory super cycle of rebuilding. When inventories get depleted and businesses must restock, this drives significant freight demand.
7677ee2524.e: Episode 31: 2026 Mid-Year State of the Freight

eea9fcf7ca.q: How are contract freight rates responding to the spot market inflation, and what percentage increases are typical?
eea9fcf7ca.a: Contract rates are resetting this cycle with increases roughly between 5% to 10%, with an average increase around 7.5% observed. However, tender rejections are higher than seen in years, with carriers competing against other opportunities, suggesting contract rates may see further increases beyond these early effects.
eea9fcf7ca.e: Episode 31: 2026 Mid-Year State of the Freight

05c0b13a11.q: What impact did recent DOT Blitz Week enforcement activity have on spot market rates and shipper behavior?
05c0b13a11.a: DOT Blitz Week was described as an absolute bloodbath, with rates doubling and tripling on some lanes. The effects were so severe that shippers questioned whether to ship product that week at all, and the rate impact carried over into following weeks.
05c0b13a11.e: Episode 31: 2026 Mid-Year State of the Freight

5d810fccf8.q: How have insurance cost pressures and cargo insurance market losses affected carrier operating expenses?
5d810fccf8.a: The cargo insurance market has continued to experience losses year-over-year, with premium increases not covering the losses insurers are experiencing. This creates ongoing pressure for further cargo insurance rate increases and impacts carrier operating costs alongside rising liability policies driven by nuclear verdicts.
5d810fccf8.e: Episode 31: 2026 Mid-Year State of the Freight

8a089e23e2.q: What regulatory changes from the SCOTUS ruling are affecting the relationship between brokers and carriers?
8a089e23e2.a: With the SCOTUS ruling, safety and vetting requirements for brokerages have increased to insulate their risk, causing many carriers to no longer be used by brokers. The days of using conditional carriers are coming to an end, though Fetch Freight has never used conditional carriers.
8a089e23e2.e: Episode 31: 2026 Mid-Year State of the Freight

f8fa9b83f1.q: What enforcement actions have targeted self-certification loopholes in CDL schools and their market impact?
f8fa9b83f1.a: FMCSA has closed north of 50 CDL schools in the southwest, Texas, and California after targeting self-certification practices that proliferated during COVID. This self-certification issue, where CDL schools prioritize commercial opportunities over adherence to requirements, has been addressed through meaningful regulatory action.
f8fa9b83f1.e: Episode 31: 2026 Mid-Year State of the Freight

82931f696d.q: What compliance steps should carriers take to maintain good standing with brokerages and avoid onboarding delays?
82931f696d.a: Carriers should keep their Certificate of Insurance (COI) current and update it with the FMCSA before expiration. They should also report new trucks to the FMCSA immediately, keep all contact information updated including phone numbers and emails, and stay proactive about maintaining accurate records. Keeping everything up to date helps save time on both ends of the onboarding process.
82931f696d.e: Episode 32: The Evolution of Freight Fraud

5a07c6c845.q: What verification methods does Fetch Freight use throughout the shipment lifecycle to protect customers from fraudulent carriers?
5a07c6c845.a: Fetch Freight collects truck and trailer plate numbers and shares them with customers so they know exactly which carrier and driver will pick up the load. They also provide real-time tracking and alert customers not to load anyone else claiming to pick up the shipment. If carrier insurance expires or a carrier falls out of good standing, Fetch notifies customers immediately to prevent liability issues.
5a07c6c845.e: Episode 32: The Evolution of Freight Fraud
